title: Data-Driven Design of Biofunctional Molecularly Imprinted Polymers for Precision Diagnostics.
summary: A learned formulation model predicted molecularly imprinted polymer nanoparticle recipes from peptide properties; candidate polymers were synthesized and tested for rebinding. This demonstrates an experimental materials-design result for the tested peptides, not clinical diagnostic performance.
ai_technology: Machine-learning formulation prediction integrated with molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics
organization: Kiel University; Hamburg University of Technology

evidence.tested: The study reports experimentally synthesized ML-predicted nanoMIP formulations and measured rebinding of targeted biomarker peptides.
evidence.unknown: The tests concern selected peptides and polymer formulations; diagnostic performance in patient samples or clinical use is not established.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning formulation prediction integrated with molecular mechanics and molecular dynamics

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
